missed: Training-time blocker not in Target A's stub list: datasets/lyft_dataset.py:121,154-168 runs config_factory('detection_lyft') and class_range.pop() on Lyft class names whenever the training LyftYawAug is constructed. The stock devkit has no such config (site-packages nuscenes/eval/detection/config.py:20-22) and DetectionConfig asserts class_range == the nuScenes DETECTION_NAMES (nuscenes/eval/detection/data_classes.py:27; overlay datasets/data_classes.py:26). The authors must have used a patched nuscenes-devkit.

Overlap-loss semantics the report does not call out (bevssl_unsupdepth.py:127-135, bevssl.py:125-126):
- The scattered volume is sparse along D: only bins that receive a projected point are non-zero.
- The mask is per pixel but is expanded over all 89 bins.
- So the SmoothL1 with an undetached target mostly regresses camera j's logits toward 0 at bins with no hit (logit shrinkage that conflicts with the BCE depth loss), rather than enforcing cross-view agreement.
- The 'dedupe' rank uses continuous depth (bevssl.py:116), so duplicates in the same (bin, v, u) cell survive and are resolved by a nondeterministic index_put.
Both matter for the faithful-vs-corrected decision.

Hard-coded camera names and layout not listed under rig assumptions: gt_vis (datasets/utils.py:188 lists 6 nuScenes/Lyft camera names; :260-263 assumes a 3+3 layout) runs at training-dataset construction (lyft_yawaug.py:26), so another rig's camera names give a KeyError. It also visualizes data_infos[-0] = data_infos[0] (utils.py:179), which is an unaugmented sample.

Two inconsistent batch derivations: reprojection uses B = BN // len(cam_pair_idx) (bevssl.py:55), while the loss uses B = BN // Ncams (bevssl_unsupdepth.py:112). With Ncams = 10, the two shapes disagree at the loss_weight AND/reshape (bevssl_unsupdepth.py:127-128) and training crashes.

Porting pitfall on the PD-BEV tree, which /home/jeongtae/Gen2E/tools/setup_env_bevdepth.sh:2-3 names as the base for vanilla BEVDepth, PD-BEV and UDGA (./bevdepth, not yet present). PD-BEV's plain PointToMultiViewDepth (PD-BEV mmdet3d/datasets/pipelines/loading.py:703-736) silently converts GT to virtual depth (f_ref=450), while LSSViewTransformerBEVDepth (mmdet3d/models/necks/view_transformer.py:590) lifts metrically. PD-BEV's own configs use PointToMultiViewDepth_UDA (loading_UDA.py:679) with LSSViewTransformer_pc. A UDGA or vanilla-BEVDepth config must pick its depth-GT path explicitly or it reproduces the same target/lifting mismatch. The setup script also effectively answers open question #9 (base = PD-BEV tree).

Environment changed after the analysis: gen2e-bevdepth and gen2e-bevformer now exist (created 2026-11-21 23:31 and 23:20; /home/jeongtae/Gen2E/logs/setup_env_bevdepth.log). gen2e-bevdepth has nuscenes-devkit 1.1.10 and lyft_dataset_sdk 0.0.8 but no mmdet3d yet.
datasets/loaders.py:177 lazily imports map_vehicle_to_car(_shift) from waymo_dataset, which is absent in master. A modified waymo_dataset.py is also missing, needed only for Waymo evaluation.

bevssl_unsupdepth.py:88-92 runs the photometric per-pair Python loops every iteration even though the term has zero gradient. It is pure compute cost and can be dropped in a port with no behavioural change.

Minor citation and version slips:
- tools/test.py:193, not :194.
- memory_profiler is imported at bevdet_uda_ft.py:14, not :13.
- bevssl.py:226-227 clamps |Δ|, not the normalized images.
- mmdet3d 1.0.0rc4 accepts mmcv-full from 1.5.2, not 1.5.3.
overall:
The report is mostly accurate and holds up when checked against the code. I confirmed the central findings independently:
- The base is BEVDet master b17b6e85 (code-identical to 4d85acf).
- The 14/22/19 file split holds.
- The listed missing modules are missing.
- The config facts are correct.
- The hard-coded 6-camera ring is as described.
- The (D,W,H) vs (D,H,W) transposition bug exists: 99.8% of points carry another pixel's logit, per my own index simulation; a torch-level run was not possible.
- The photometric loss has no gradient.
- The pixel_const target is d/k while lifting uses bin/k. I checked this against DG-BEV Eq. 3-4 (PDF p.4) and PD-BEV's code.
- extaug never moves the LiDAR points into the rotated frame.
- The adapter/PEFT parameters are unregistered and the requries_grad typos are real.
- The paper facts check out: BEVFormer gets adapters only, 24 epochs, ±50 m, NDS* formula.

Three things need correcting:
1. The 'detection_lyft' devkit config and LyftEval are wrongly scoped as "Lyft-as-target only". They block stage-1 training and even package import. A Lyft-class eval config also needs a patched nuscenes-devkit (DETECTION_NAMES assert), not just a JSON. Target A's stub list omits this.
2. The NaN-on-empty-mask risk is overstated. The mask is pooled over all pairs and the whole batch, so a single non-overlapping pair does not produce NaN.
3. The environment section is stale. gen2e-bevdepth and gen2e-bevformer were created after the analysis. The mmcv lower bound for rc4 is 1.5.2, not 1.5.3.

The most important omissions:
- The L1 overlap loss mostly pulls the target camera's logits toward 0 at bins with no hit.
- gt_vis hard-codes the camera names and runs during training-dataset construction.
- The two batch-size derivations disagree and crash on non-5/6-camera rigs.
- The project's own setup script builds the UDGA port on the PD-BEV tree. That tree's plain PointToMultiViewDepth silently produces virtual-depth GT, so a careless port would reintroduce the same target/lifting inconsistency.

The effort estimates are judgment calls; Target A's M looks optimistic. The license reading (no public GitHub release without Samsung's permission) matches the LICENSE text, though its legal effect cannot be verified here.
